Chief_Complaint.content: Episodic right hand pins and needles, numbness, perceived right arm weakness, and intermittent leg weakness with abnormal gait
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Episodic R hand pins/needles and numbness; perceived R arm weakness; intermittent leg weakness with abnormal gait noted by colleague

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Neurologic symptoms began approximately 1.5 to 2 months ago
Initially symptoms occurred about once per week to once per month
Symptom frequency has increased to a couple of times per day
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: now ↑ freq to a couple times/day

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Each episode lasts approximately 3–4 days then resolves
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: each episode lasts ~3–4 days then resolves

History_of_Present_Illness.content: During episodes, has difficulty holding a cup and finds it slightly harder to drink
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: during episodes: difficulty holding cup, slightly harder to drink

History_of_Present_Illness.content: During episodes, feels something in his throat
No prior history of TIA or stroke
Previous blood pressure, cholesterol, and diabetes mellitus tests reported as okay

Medications.content: Aspirin 75 mg once daily, self-initiated for stroke and myocardial infarction prevention
Medications.source_text: Meds: Aspirin 75 mg OD (self-initiated for stroke/MI prevention)

Family_History.content: Father had carotid artery operation to reduce stroke risk
Family_History.source_text: FH: father had carotid artery operation to reduce stroke risk

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a doctor in plastic surgery

Assessment.content: Recurrent transient neurologic episodes with right hand paresthesia and weakness, concurrent leg weakness and gait change, and transient difficulty drinking with family history of cerebrovascular disease, concerning for transient ischemic attack
Assessment.source_text: 1) Recurrent transient neurologic episodes (R hand paresthesia/weakness; concurrent leg weakness/gait change; transient difficulty drinking; FH cerebrovascular disease). Concern for TIA.

Plan_of_Care.content: Expected TIA clinic appointment within 1–2 days, by Thursday or Friday
In TIA clinic, carotid ultrasound with or without brain imaging is anticipated
Plan_of_Care.source_text: In clinic: carotid US +/- brain imaging anticipated

Plan_of_Care.content: Provide TIA clinic and PALS contact numbers so patient can call to confirm booking and ensure he is listed
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Provide TIA clinic and PALS contact numbers; pt to call today/tomorrow to confirm booking and ensure listed

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise patient to contact GP if there are delays or if he is unable to attend the appointment
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Contact GP if delays or unable to attend appointment

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to call TIA clinic and PALS today or tomorrow to confirm booking and ensure he is listed
Follow_up_Information.source_text: pt to call today/tomorrow to confirm booking and ensure listed

Follow_up_Information.content: If symptoms recur and are prolonged or persistent, patient should attend A&E immediately
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Safety-net: if symptoms recur and are prolonged/persistent → attend A&E immediately
